title: Drag files to apps, safer Windows transfers, and easier editing
notes: On Windows, Drag to last used app lets you send the selected file or folder into another application with a guided drag-and-drop action. You can steer the cursor with the keyboard, and the new Help button shows the controls.

Windows users can now copy or move files with native Robocopy support. Choose a destination in the other pane or enter a local or UNC path, with configurable retries, threading and optional transfer logs.
Set text editor now helps you configure your editor with ready-made presets or your own arguments. You can run it from the command palette, including while viewing a file.
When one item is selected, you can copy just its file name or full path to the clipboard. These commands also work from the viewer.
Open native file manager now works from the network overview and from individual network computers, taking you directly to the matching Windows Explorer location.
Transfer prompts and Windows message boxes are easier to read: destination errors are clearer, and dialogs with several buttons no longer collapse into a narrow column.
